import plotly.graph_objects as go

    'Year': [2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019],

    'Air Cargo Logistics': [10.2, 10.8, 11.1, 11.5, 11.9, 12.3, 12.8, 13.2, 13.7, 14.1],
    'Heavy Road Freight': [8.3, 8.5, 8.7, 9.1, 9.4, 9.6, 9.9, 10.2, 10.5, 10.8],

    y=data['Domestic Passenger Air'],

The cumulative economic impact of all sectors combined reaches nearly 100 billion USD by 2019, demonstrating steady growth across the decade. from pathlib import Path
import runpy
import pandas as pd

source = Path("chart.py").read_text()
source = source.replace(
    "y=data['Maritime Shipping'],\n    mode='lines',\n    name='International Passenger Air',",
    "y=data['Maritime Shipping'],\n    mode='lines',\n    name='Maritime Shipping',"
)
source = source.replace(
    "y=data['International Passenger Air'],\n    mode='lines',\n    name='Maritime Shipping',\n    stackgroup='one',\n    line=dict(width=0.5, color='#ff7f0e')",
    "y=data['International Passenger Air'],\n    mode='lines',\n    name='International Passenger Air',\n    stackgroup='one',\n    line=dict(width=0.5, color='#c49c94')"
)
Path("chart.py").write_text(source)
state = runpy.run_path("chart.py")
fig = state["fig"]
print(pd.read_csv("table.csv").to_string(index=False))
print("\nVerified trace names, colors, and data correspondence:")
for trace in fig.data:
    assert list(trace.y) == state["data"][trace.name]
    print(trace.name, trace.line.color)
assert fig.data[0].name == "Maritime Shipping"
assert fig.data[4].name == "International Passenger Air"
assert fig.data[4].line.color == "#c49c94"
